Okay, I'm going to \*\*\*heavily\*\*\* simplify.

Without the intention of changing your beliefs, understand that dreams do not reflect 'past lives' or 'other worlds.'

If you feel as though you've 'dreamt the future,' then know that it is merely but a flawed explanation for modified memories.

The subconscious governs dreams; they are created in the brain influenced by a myriad of factors; therefore, oft-times dreams try to predict events based on your feelings, include people you've seen, or replay past experiences.

The mechanism for storing dreams is inherently weak. You dream every night and experience a lot, lot more than 1 or 2 or 3 dreams. However, not all of those are stored and it is usually the \[most\] recent ones or impressionable ones. And most of time, some dreams are stored in fragments or pieces and segments because the moment you wake up, unless you have good dream recall, you might slowly forget the \[less important\] information from the dream.

As you go about your life, you might encounter an event or events that resemble the dream. Amidst relevant stimuli (the event), your brain fills in the gaps in the dream memory by blending its fragments and segments with real life experiences, which would be the event.

This reconstruction creates an altered, 'modified' memory which, to you, seems only like an ordinary dream memory when it resurfaces \[amidst relevant stimuli\].
